title: Bread Sauce
subtitle: Creamy milk and breadcrumb sauce for roast chicken
excerpt: Whole milk infused with onion, bay, cloves, and black pepper, thickened with white breadcrumbs and finished with butter and cream. The essential British condiment for roast chicken and turkey.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bread sauce is one of Britain's oldest surviving sauces, with roots going back to medieval pottages. In an era before potatoes were widely available, bread was used as a thickener for nearly every sauce and soup. The method of infusing milk with aromatics before adding breadcrumbs dates to at least the 17th century. Despite its medieval origins, bread sauce has remained on British Christmas tables essentially unchanged. It is almost always served with roast chicken or turkey and is one of the few sauces that is genuinely British rather than adapted from French cuisine.

content.text: The infusing stage is critical: the longer the milk sits with the aromatics, the more flavour the sauce will have. Thirty minutes is the minimum; an hour is better. Use day-old white bread for the breadcrumbs: fresh bread will make the sauce gluey, and brown bread will make it grey. The sauce thickens considerably as it stands: loosen with a splash of warm milk before serving.

items.preparation: day-old, crusts removed, blitzed to breadcrumbs

content.text: Put the milk in a saucepan with the onion halves (studded with the cloves), bay leaves, and peppercorns. Bring just to a simmer over low heat. Remove from the heat. Cover and leave to infuse for at least 30 minutes.
Strain the milk into a clean saucepan, discarding the onion and aromatics. Return to low heat.

Stir in the breadcrumbs. Cook over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the sauce is thick and smooth. Stir in the butter and cream. Season with salt and nutmeg. Keep warm over the lowest heat, stirring occasionally. Loosen with a little warm milk if needed before serving.
